notes.content: DIVERSITY REQUIREMENT FOR CAL STATE LA GRADUATION

The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement , not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University. For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements. Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

notes.content: Overview The Bachelor of Arts degree program in Liberal Studies offers four options. The Liberal Studies major is named in California law as the preferred degree for students who wish to teach in elementary schools. As such, Liberal Studies offers two options in elementary subject matter teacher preparation, including an Integrated Teacher Education Preparation (ITEP) program that combines the credential with undergraduate coursework. The Liberal Studies major also has two career-focused interdisciplinary options where students have a great deal of flexibility to customize their coursework. All Liberal Studies options place a strong emphasis on developing student skills in composition, information literacy, cultural literacy, and analysis across disciplines, contexts, and media. Advisement All students who intend to major in Liberal Studies should confer with a College of Arts and Letters or Liberal Studies faculty advisor by the end of the first semester of residence in order to select an option, establish an official degree program, and develop an academic plan. Options Option I - Elementary Subject Matter Teacher Preparation: Traditional Option provides students a broad-based education in multiple subjects that can include a waiver for the California Subject Examinations for Teachers: Multiple Subjects (CSET: MS). A grade of C or higher is required in all major core courses and all Elementary Subject Matter courses. Students who select Option I must complete 21 units of elementary subject matter courses from the categories listed below (3000-4000 level courses). Students should consult with a College of Arts and Letters or Department of Liberal Studies adviser to ensure they have completed all courses required for the CSET: Multiple Subjects waiver. Option II - Integrated Teacher Education Program also known as the ITEP option, provides qualified students the opportunity to complete the requirements for a Multiple Subjects or Special Education teaching credential while completing the requirements for the Bachelor of Arts degree. Students in Option II can take coursework that can lead to a waiver for the California Subject Examinations for Teachers ( CSET ) Multiple Subjects. Particular requirements and restrictions apply to candidates for teaching. Therefore, early consultation with a College of Arts and Letters or Liberal Studies faculty advisor is essential. Refer to the College of Education section of this catalog for regulations governing all teaching credential programs. Students in Option II must also complete additional coursework in Multiple Subject or Education Specialist credentials. Option III - Interdisciplinary Studies in Culture and Society offers students the opportunity to pursue an integrative interdisciplinary course of study that will provide them with a broad base of knowledge and skills through a depth area in American Studies, Environmental Justice and Sustainability, or Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies. The knowledge and skills developed in this option prepare students for careers in fields such as education, law, journalism, publishing, government, business, and non-profit work. Option IV - Applied and Professional Humanities offers students the opportunity to design a program of study with a faculty advisor that suits their unique personal and professional interests. This option can include a wide range of coursework, minors, certificates, and micro-credentials geared toward developing career skills and knowledge appropriate for the jobs of the twenty-first century. Requirements for the Major The Liberal Studies core requirements are designed to provide the necessary analytical framework, including rhetorical skills, theoretical concepts, research methods, and techniques of argumentation to enable students to master each of the available options in the Liberal Studies major. In addition to the core courses, students are required to complete take 9 units of Liberal Studies breadth Courses, of which, 6 units in the Intermediate Interdisciplinary Studies category are double-counted for upper division general education requirements.

Overview

The Bachelor of Arts degree program in Liberal Studies offers four options. The Liberal Studies major is named in California law as the preferred degree for students who wish to teach in elementary schools. As such, Liberal Studies offers two options in elementary subject matter teacher preparation, including an Integrated Teacher Education Preparation (ITEP) program that combines the credential with undergraduate coursework.

The Liberal Studies major also has two career-focused interdisciplinary options where students have a great deal of flexibility to customize their coursework. All Liberal Studies options place a strong emphasis on developing student skills in composition, information literacy, cultural literacy, and analysis across disciplines, contexts, and media.

Advisement

All students who intend to major in Liberal Studies should confer with a College of Arts and Letters or Liberal Studies faculty advisor by the end of the first semester of residence in order to select an option, establish an official degree program, and develop an academic plan.

Options

  • Option I - Elementary Subject Matter Teacher Preparation: Traditional Option provides students a broad-based education in multiple subjects that can include a waiver for the California Subject Examinations for Teachers: Multiple Subjects (CSET: MS). A grade of C or higher is required in all major core courses and all Elementary Subject Matter courses.
  • Students who select Option I must complete 21 units of elementary subject matter courses from the categories listed below (3000-4000 level courses). Students should consult with a College of Arts and Letters or Department of Liberal Studies adviser to ensure they have completed all courses required for the CSET: Multiple Subjects waiver. 
  • Option II - Integrated Teacher Education Program also known as the ITEP option, provides qualified students the opportunity to complete the requirements for a Multiple Subjects or Special Education teaching credential while completing the requirements for the Bachelor of Arts degree. Students in Option II can take coursework that can lead to a waiver for the California Subject Examinations for Teachers (CSET) Multiple Subjects. Particular requirements and restrictions apply to candidates for teaching. Therefore, early consultation with a College of Arts and Letters or Liberal Studies faculty advisor is essential. Refer to the College of Education section of this catalog for regulations governing all teaching credential programs.  Students in Option II must also complete additional coursework in Multiple Subject or Education Specialist credentials.
  • Option III - Interdisciplinary Studies in Culture and Society offers students the opportunity to pursue an integrative interdisciplinary course of study that will provide them with a broad base of knowledge and skills through a depth area in American Studies, Environmental Justice and Sustainability, or Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies. The knowledge and skills developed in this option prepare students for careers in fields such as education, law, journalism, publishing, government, business, and non-profit work.
  • Option IV - Applied and Professional Humanities offers students the opportunity to design a program of study with a faculty advisor that suits their unique personal and professional interests. This option can include a wide range of coursework, minors, certificates, and micro-credentials geared toward developing career skills and knowledge appropriate for the jobs of the twenty-first century.

Requirements for the Major

  • The Liberal Studies core requirements are designed to provide the necessary analytical framework, including rhetorical skills, theoretical concepts, research methods, and techniques of argumentation to enable students to master each of the available options in the Liberal Studies major. 
  • In addition to the core courses, students are required to complete take 9 units of Liberal Studies breadth Courses, of which, 6 units in the Intermediate Interdisciplinary Studies category are double-counted for upper division general education requirements.
